name: Hip mobility for running
summary: 18-minute routine for the hips a runner needs: hip flexors and rotation for stride length, glute medius for pelvic control (it also takes load off the ankle and the posterior tibial area), and a deep squat to finish. Slow and controlled — this is mobility, not a workout.
equipment: Mat. Optional: mini band, light kettlebell or dumbbell.
when_to_use: Easy or rest days, after an easy run, or the evening before a long run. Not straight before a hard session — do leg swings only then.

exercises.name: Front-to-back leg swings
cues: Hold a wall, stand tall on one leg
Swing the free leg forward and back, letting the range grow
Keep the pelvis level and the torso quiet
exercises.why: Dynamic warm-up for the hip flexors and hamstrings.

exercises.name: Side-to-side leg swings
cues: Face the wall, hands on it
Swing the leg across your body and out to the side
Hips square to the wall
exercises.why: Opens the adductors and abductors before the floor work.

exercises.name: 90/90 hip switches
cues: Sit with both knees bent to 90°, one leg in front, one to the side
Rotate both knees to the other side without using your hands if you can
Sit tall; pause 2 s at each end
exercises.why: Internal and external hip rotation — the range that goes first in long-distance runners.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
cues: Back knee down on a mat, front foot flat
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck the pelvis
Shift forward only until you feel the front of the hip — don't arch the low back
Reach the same-side arm overhead to deepen it
exercises.why: Hours of sitting plus running shorten the hip flexors and cut stride length.

exercises.name: World's greatest stretch
cues: Long lunge, back knee off the floor
Same-side elbow down towards the instep
Rotate and reach that arm to the ceiling, eyes follow the hand
Return, step through, switch sides
exercises.why: Hip flexor, adductor, hamstring and thoracic rotation in one move.

exercises.name: Cossack squat
cues: Wide stance, toes slightly out
Sit into one hip while the other leg straightens, toes up
Heel stays down, chest up; hold a support if needed
Only as deep as you can control
exercises.why: Lateral hip and adductor strength-through-range — downhill running loads these.

exercises.name: Pigeon stretch (or figure-4 on your back)
cues: Front shin across the mat, back leg long behind
Square the hips and fold forward slowly
Knee or hip pain: switch to figure-4 lying on your back
exercises.why: Glutes and deep hip rotators, which tighten with mileage.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: Feet hip-width, heels close to the bum
Push through the heels, squeeze the glutes, ribs down
Hold 2 s at the top; don't arch the low back
exercises.why: Wakes up the glutes so they, not the hamstrings and low back, drive hip extension.

exercises.name: Clamshell
cues: Lie on your side, knees bent, heels together
Lift the top knee without rolling the pelvis back
Slow down, 1 s pause at the top; add a mini band when easy
exercises.why: Glute medius control — stops the knee caving in and the foot over-pronating.

exercises.name: Side-lying hip abduction
cues: Bottom leg bent, top leg straight in line with the body
Lift the top leg slightly behind you, toes pointing forward (not up)
Lower slowly over 3 s
exercises.why: The glute medius again, in the straight-leg position you run in.

exercises.name: Deep squat hold
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, heels down
Sit deep, elbows push the knees out, chest up
Hold a light weight in front or a door frame for balance
Breathe slowly and shift side to side
exercises.why: Ankle, knee and hip range together — finishes the session in a position your hips rarely see.
